strategy.summary: Two operations in openapi.yaml have no test: GET /products/{id} (getProduct) and POST /orders/{id}/cancel (cancelOrder). Add tests of each one's success response and every error response the spec documents (404 for both, plus 409 for cancelling an order that is already cancelled). Each test checks the status, the JSON content type and the body shape the spec gives. Also, the existing GET /orders/{id} test still checks the old `totalCents` field. The spec (and commit bef1422) now returns `total` as a Money object, so that assertion is updated to the current contract.
inScope: Updating the existing GET /orders/{id} success assertion to the spec's Order schema (total: Money), keeping everything else it checks
outOfScope: Changes to the spec or the application
Behaviour the spec does not document (e.g. stock returned on cancel)
Restructuring existing tests beyond the ticket's needs (e.g. extracting the duplicated server setup); listed as a follow-up
assumptions: The tests start the real app in-process with createApp() on port 0, as the existing specs do. Nothing is faked: the app has an in-memory store and no external services.

New cases go into the existing test/products.test.js and test/orders.test.js beside the operations' siblings, reusing each file's server setup, so no setup code is copied. Each file gets the ticket tag comment listing its cases.
Expected product values come from PRODUCTS, imported from src/store.js, rather than being written out by hand.

risks.description: Tests in one file share a store, so orders and stock changes from one test can be seen by another
risks.mitigation: Each cancel test places its own order and asserts only on that order's id. Product reads assert stock only by type.

review.standard: Keeping API tests in step with the spec: assert the contract (properties and their types); Assert the one outcome the app produces
review.summary: The getProduct 200 test checks `stock` with `expect.any(Number)`. That accepts a non-integer, but the spec's Product.stock is an integer (and TC1 expects `stock: integer`). In this file's own fresh store the value is fixed, because nothing in products.test.js changes stock.
review.failureScenario: Suppose GET /products/2 returned the wrong stock, such as 0 or 4.5 instead of the Teapot's 4. `expect.any(Number)` still matches, so the test passes while the response breaks the spec's integer type or reports the wrong stock. Because createApp() builds a fresh store per file and no test in products.test.js places orders, the test could assert `stock: teapot.stock`. At least it should check `Number.isInteger(body.stock)`.
